title: Two Pointers Technique
intuition: Coordinating two indices that traverse a data structure simultaneously to avoid nested loops.
whyExists: Transforms brute-force $O(n^2)$ pair problems into optimal $O(n)$ single-pass solutions by exploiting sorted monotonicity.
analogy: Two people walking towards each other from opposite ends of a bridge to meet at a designated rendezvous point.
coreIdea: Typically initializes left = 0 and right = n - 1 on a sorted array. The sum a[left] + a[right] is tested against target. Because the array is sorted, incrementing left is guaranteed to increase the sum, and decrementing right is guaranteed to decrease the sum.

complexity.reason: In every step, at least one pointer moves inwards; at most n steps total.

pitfalls: Applying converging two pointers to an unsorted array without sorting first.
Infinite loop if neither pointer is guaranteed to advance on every step.
Index out of bounds when pointer movement conditions fail to check left < right.
